learn.title: Place value
learn.body: A decimal extends our number system to parts smaller than 1. In $3.746$ the digits after the point are tenths (7), hundredths (4) and thousandths (6). Each place is ten times smaller than the one to its left.

learn.title: Fractions and decimals
learn.body: A decimal is a fraction with a denominator of 10, 100, 1000 and so on. $0.75=\frac{75}{100}=\frac{3}{4}$. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide: $\frac{1}{8}=1\div 8=0.125$. Some decimals repeat forever, like $\frac{1}{3}=0.333\ldots$

learn.title: Adding and multiplying
learn.body: To add or subtract, line up the decimal points: $4.5+2.35=6.85$. To multiply, ignore the points, multiply, then count the decimal places in the factors. $0.3\times 0.2$: $3\times 2=6$, with two decimal places, gives $0.06$.

learn.title: Round $3.746$ to 2 decimal places
learn.body: Look at the digit just after the place you keep.
steps: Keep two decimals: $3.74$ and look at the next digit, 6.
6 is 5 or more, so round the last kept digit up.

learn.body: The rule for rounding: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less leaves the digit alone. $3.742$ would round to $3.74$.

questions.prompt: In $3.746$, what is the digit 7 worth?
questions.explanation: The first place after the point is tenths, so the 7 means $\frac{7}{10}$.
The next digit is 6, so round the 4 up to 5.
$3\times 2=6$ and there are two decimal places in total, so $0.06$.
Compare place by place. $0.5=0.50$, which is more than $0.45$ and $0.095$.

questions.prompt: Match each fraction with its decimal.
questions.explanation: Divide the top by the bottom: $1\div 2=0.5$, $1\div 4=0.25$, $1\div 8=0.125$.
